channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Spain’s new anti-smoking law: All you need to know about where you can no longer light up – including bar terrace ban
item.description: Spain’s new anti-smoking law shows how easily tobacco control can expand from protecting bystanders to restricting every nicotine product in the same breath. Smoke-free spaces, youth protection and advertising rules all deserve serious attention, but policy loses precision when cigarettes, vapes and heated tobacco are treated as one problem. The goal should be less smoking and less exposure to harmful emissions, not a framework that blurs the difference between combustion and lower-risk alternatives. Strong regulation works best when it understands what it is regulating. (Published on September 28, 2026bytheolivepress.es)

item.title: Decisive Move | Haypp Goes All-In on U.S. Nicotine Pouch Market | RegWatch
item.description: Haypp’s move into the US nicotine pouch market reflects more than business expansion. It signals growing consumer demand for smoke-free products that are convenient, discreet and separate from combustion. That shift matters because markets can either be shaped through responsible standards or left to develop without enough oversight. A strong harm reduction framework should make room for adult access, product accountability and clear information about where pouches sit on the risk spectrum. (Published on September 28, 2026byregulatorwatch.com)

item.title: Vape prohibitions: an interview
item.description: Vape prohibitions promise control, but their real legacy is often a messier market. Legal products disappear from view, illicit sellers gain room to operate, and adult smokers lose one of the most accessible routes away from cigarettes. The policy may look firm, yet the behaviour it tries to stop simply moves elsewhere. Harm reduction starts from that reality: people need safer options that are legal, regulated and easier to choose than the dangerous ones. (Published on September 28, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Nicotine Risk Insurance Pricing: What Reinsurers Say
item.description: Insurance pricing can reveal how poorly nicotine risk is understood. Treating every nicotine user like a smoker ignores the difference between combustible tobacco and smoke-free alternatives such as pouches, snus or vaping. That matters because premiums can punish people who have reduced their risk by leaving cigarettes behind. A fairer approach would price risk according to evidence, exposure and product type — not according to nicotine use alone. (Published on September 28, 2026bytobaccoharmreduction.net)

item.title: Major review finds nicotine pouches considerably less toxic than cigarettes
item.description: Toxicity is where the nicotine debate needs less rhetoric and more comparison. A major review finding nicotine pouches considerably less toxic than cigarettes reinforces the basic harm reduction point: the way nicotine is delivered changes the risk profile. Smoke-free does not mean risk-free, but it does mean the absence of combustion and far lower exposure to many harmful toxicants. Policy should reflect that difference instead of treating pouches and cigarettes as interchangeable threats. (Published on September 28, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)
